The season ran from 23 February to 20 October 2002. [[Atlético Petróleos de Luanda|Petro de Luanda]] were the defending champions. The league comprised 14 teams, the bottom three of which were relegated to the 2003 [[Gira Angola]]. [[Atlético Sport Aviação|ASA]] were crowned champions, winning their first title,{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/pt_pt/noticias/desporto/2002/9/43/,c50a71d5-afcb-46a0-925e-52b4b6365642.html |title=O Atlético Sport Aviação (Asa) conquistou o primeiro título |publisher=ANGOP.com |date=21 Oct 2002 |access-date=6 Dec 2014 |language=pt |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304073610/http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/pt_pt/noticias/desporto/2002/9/43/,c50a71d5-afcb-46a0-925e-52b4b6365642.html |url-status=dead }} while [[S.L. Benfica (Lubango)|Benfica do Lubango]], [[F.C. Cabinda|Futebol Clube de Cabinda]] and [[Sporting Clube Petróleos do Bié|Sporting do Bié]], were relegated. [[Flávio Amado]] of [[Atlético Petróleos de Luanda|Petro de Luanda]] finished as the top scorer with 16 goals.{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/pt_pt/noticias/desporto/2002/10/46/,45a9f2a8-bbd4-43e2-b0c8-fc6c55365235.html |title=O avançado do Petro de Luanda, Flávio Amado, melhor marcador do campeonato nacional de futebol da Iª divisão "Girabola-2002" |publisher=ANGOP.com |date=15 Nov 2002 |access-date=13 Sep 2015}} ==Changes from the 2001 season== '''Relegated:''' [[F.C.
